transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-06-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Elliot Park (CTO, NovaForge), Sana Ibrahim (ML Engineer, NovaForge), Marcus Lee (Infra Lead, NovaForge)

Summary: NovaForge wants a fast path to prototype LLM features via Redwood's hosted API with free credits, then evaluate Dedicated or Private for production due to PII and residency requirements. They value developer experience and short TTFT, and want to understand security options and pilot economics.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood side, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. Could we quick intros from NovaForge?
[00:07] Elliot (NovaForge): Sure, I'm Elliot, CTO at NovaForge. We build an API-first product for enterprise supply chain data, lots of structured docs and some sensitive client PII so security is top of mind.
[00:14] Sana (NovaForge): Sana, ML engineer, I'll own the prototype and run experiments with prompt templates.
[00:18] Marcus (NovaForge): Marcus, infra lead, I'll want to understand VPC/private options and network flow.
[00:23] Jordan: Awesome. We scheduled this to cover quickstart flow, credits, time-to-first-token, and then where Dedicated or Private might come in for you. Quick question — are you planning to start as purely self-serve or do you expect sales assist right away?
[00:36] Elliot: We want to move fast; ideally self-serve for proof-of-concept. But if we see heavy usage or residency concerns we'll escalate. Our PM wants devs to be able to hit a working endpoint within a day.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Great — that aligns with our PLG path. With our hosted API we typically enable TTFT in under a few hours for dev environments: signup, free credits, API key, example repo. How many devs would be on the experiment?
[01:00] Sana: Two to three initially. We'll run evals on ~50 sample documents and some structured extraction tasks.
[01:06] Jordan: Perfect. For the credits — we can provide a short trial allocation that covers your early tests; if you want a reserved commitment for a pilot we can invoice a small pilot deposit that converts to credits.
[01:16] Elliot: What does that look like cost-wise? Also we want to compare latency vs cost — we care about sub-200ms token latency for interactive features but okay with higher for batch.
[01:27] Priya: For hosted, latency depends on model and sequence length; our smaller open models can hit sub-200ms median for single-turn requests with short context. If you need consistent p95 bounds you might consider Dedicated. But for prototyping hosted gives fastest TTFT and easiest path.
[01:44] Marcus: On the security side, our legal team asked about SOC 2, SSO and KMS. We need to know if logs or payloads can be restricted or encrypted.
[01:52] Jordan: Yes — we have SOC 2 and enterprise SSO (SAML/SCIM) for accounts. For hosted, you can enable token redaction and short retention or opt into Private for full customer-managed KMS/HSM. We can share our security pack after this call.
[02:05] Sana: Quick tech Q — will we lose ability to use KV cache or embeddings if we start hosted?
[02:11] Priya: Not at all; hosted supports embeddings and prefix/K-V caching. Apologies, sometimes transcript says K-V cash, but it's KV cache. For Dedicated/Private, you get more control over cache placement and latency.
[02:23] Elliot: Ok. We want to measure quality regressions as we tune quantization and batching. How do you recommend we instrument that?
[02:31] Priya: We have an Optimize toolkit that recommends batching and quantization per workload and also evaluation hooks you can add to track prompt sets. We'll share a sample eval harness and you can run baseline metrics.
[02:41] Jordan: To make this concrete: we'll send a starter repo with curl examples, SDK snippets, and a short checklist to reach TTFT. Priya will also include a light benchmark script to run against hosted and some baseline numbers.
[02:52] Marcus: Network-wise, if we later go Private, what's the onboarding like? We use a VPC with strict egress rules.
[02:59] Priya: For Private we do a VPC peering or private link setup; there's a short network checklist — allow certain outbound IPs or set up private endpoints. We'll need your network diagram to validate. The onboarding for Private takes longer (weeks) vs hosted (hours).
[03:11] Elliot: That matches our expectation. For pilot acceptance criteria — we want 1) reproducible extraction on sample dataset, 2) latency within X for interactive features (we'll define exact number), and 3) no PII persisted beyond retention windows.
[03:25] Jordan: Good criteria. We'll map those to pilot success metrics. For retention and encryption: hosted has configurable retention and optional encryption in transit and at rest; Dedicated gives you stronger isolation; Private gives you customer-managed keys and full audit logs.
[03:42] Sana: Regarding developer flow — can we onboard via self-serve, or do we need a Redwood rep?
[03:47] Jordan: You can self-serve: sign up, get API key, drop in the quickstart repo. But since you have infra/security considerations we'll run a parallel review — so you'll get both the self-serve path and an SE check-in.
[03:59] Marcus: About data residency — some customers require EU-only processing. Do you have regional endpoints?
[04:05] Priya: Yes, we have region routing and can pin requests to EU regions — for hosted, we offer EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated/Private in your region. We'll flag region in the pilot SOW.
[04:18] Elliot: Any known gotchas with JSON schema and structured outputs? Our pipeline expects strict JSON output from the model.
[04:24] Priya: We support structured output with model function calling and schema enforcement patterns. For early runs you'll likely use our streaming endpoint and post-process; we can also provide prompt templates for schema extraction.
[04:36] Sana: Can we run a quick perf test today? I can run a small script if you give sample curl and an API key.
[04:42] Jordan: We can enable a short-lived trial key now but we'll follow with an official credit allocation. For security, we'll also give you sample logs so you know what gets retained.
[04:52] Elliot: On the competitor side, we also looked at Anthropic and OpenAI hosted APIs. The main differentiator for us is run cost and ability to move to private infra later without reworking APIs.
[05:02] Priya: Right — our API is consistent across hosting modes so migration is much smoother. We also provide rollout tools (canaries, fallbacks) which help in production.
[05:12] Jordan: Let's walk a little through the quickstart steps — sign up, create API key, try sample prompt, run embedding job, and try a small batch. Priya, do you want to call out the repo?
[05:21] Priya: The repo has step-by-step notebooks and a tiny benchmark harness. It's designed to get you to TTFT in under two hours for a single dev. Typical friction points: private network rules, long sequence lengths increasing token latency, and initial prompt engineering.
[05:34] Marcus: If we hit heavy token usage, what's the billing model? Per-token tiered or dedicated capacity?
[05:39] Jordan: Hosted is per-token with tiered volume discounts. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and predictable throughput — lower unit cost at scale. We can show a modeled comparison once you share expected qps and context lengths.
[05:53] Sana: For the pilot, we'll start with 10k tokens/day equivalent to profile costs. Can we get an estimate?
[05:59] Jordan: We'll give a tailored estimate in the pricing sheet. For now, our pilot credit allocation should cover your first runs.
[06:06] Elliot: About audit logs and access controls — we need RBAC and SSO for the team.
[06:11] Priya: Enterprise accounts support SAML SSO and role-based permissions. Logs can be exported to your SIEM or we can provide retention policy. Private gives full customer-controlled audit trail.
[06:23] Marcus: Our security folks will request encryption with customer-managed keys. Is HSM supported?
[06:29] Jordan: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key options. For Hosted we manage keys but can support stronger encryption policies and limited retention.
[06:41] Sana: Small note — we've seen transcription systems mis-label product names; please assume Redwood Dedication = Redwood Dedicated in the notes.
[06:47] Priya: Ha, yes — the transcript sometimes mangles names. We'll make sure docs are clear.
[06:53] Jordan: Any blockers to starting the self-serve quickstart today?
[06:58] Elliot: From our side no blockers — we want the credit allocation and the quickstart repo. The legal/compliance review will run in parallel; we'll need security docs.
[07:06] Jordan: We'll send the security pack and pilot SOW. Priya will include a checklist and sample scripts.
[07:11] --- (longer technical exchange, 07:12-35:00) ---
[07:12] Priya: Walkthrough of the sample curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-mini-1","input":"Extract invoice fields"}' ... you get the idea.
[07:25] Sana: Running the harness now, noticing a variance at p95 with longer contexts. Is the runtime doing kernel selection?
[07:32] Priya: Yes, runtime does kernel selection and continuous batching. For your profile we'll recommend a quantization profile and smaller sequence chunking. That reduces p95 and cost.
[07:45] Marcus: If we schedule a Dedicated pilot, timeline is about how long?
[07:49] Priya: Dedicated ramp is typically 2-4 weeks to provision and tune; Private longer due to networking and KMS setup — typically 4-8 weeks. But again, you can start hosted immediately.
[08:00] Sana: For evaluation hooks, can we forward logs to our Sentry or Datadog?
[08:05] Priya: Yes, you can export traces and token-level metrics to Datadog or BigQuery for analysis.
[08:12] (crosstalk)
[08:14] Elliot: Ok let's put tentative dates — pilot kickoff week of June 11th and a 3-week pilot.
[08:19] Jordan: Noted. We'll provision credits and get the SOW over.
[08:22] --- (mid-call clarifications and small interruptions) ---
[20:05] Sana: A few more specifics — do you have SDKs for Python/Go/Node?
[20:10] Priya: Yes, official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. They include streaming and embeddings helpers.
[20:16] Marcus: For private deployment we have strict egress. Can Redwood run in our on-prem air-gapped environment?
[20:22] Priya: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments but it's more of an enterprise engagement; it requires additional security review and licensing.
[20:30] Elliot: How does rollback work for model rollouts? We need canary and fallback to cheaper models if latency spikes.
[20:36] Jordan: We support canary deploys and automatic fallback policies. You can route by latency or cost and fall back to a smaller model.
[20:44] Sana: For prompt-based extraction we need strong determinism for certain fields — any guidance?
[20:48] Priya: Use structured function calls or scoring rerank; include few-shot examples and temperature low for determinism. We'll share prompt recipes.
[21:00] --- closing  parts of call ---
[47:30] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll send pilot pricing and SOW, quickstart repo and runbook, a small benchmark script and security pack. You (NovaForge) will confirm datasets and success criteria and share network diagram. We tentatively plan pilot kickoff week of 2028-06-11.
[47:52] Elliot: Sounds good. Marcus will get the network diagram and Sana will run the quickstart. We'll review security docs with our compliance team.
[48:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Priya and I will follow up with the artifacts and schedule a 30-min tech kickoff.
[48:08] Elliot: Thank you.
[48:10] (call ends)
